--- Dockerfile ---
FROM python:3.11
ENV PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1
ENV PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1
## DEV variables start
ARG DEV_GNE_AUTHENTICATION_TOKEN
ENV DEV_GNE_AUTHENTICATION_TOKEN=$DEV_GNE_AUTHENTICATION_TOKEN

ARG DEV_GNE_AUTHORIZATION_TOKEN
ENV DEV_GNE_AUTHORIZATION_TOKEN=$DEV_GNE_AUTHORIZATION_TOKEN

COPY requirements/container.txt ./
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir --upgrade -r container.txt
ENV APP_HOME=/app
WORKDIR $APP_HOME
# Feel free to rename "api" to specific name of your API. example - product_compatibility
COPY api $APP_HOME/api
RUN useradd -ms /bin/bash appuser
USER appuser
CMD ["fastapi", "run", "api/main.py", "--port", "8080"]

--- bitbucket-pipelines.yml ---
image: maven:3.6.3-jdk-11
clone:
  depth: full 
definitions:
  caches:
    sonar: ~/.sonar/cache  # Caching SonarCloud artifacts will speed up your build
  steps:
    - step: &MetadataCheck
        image: google/cloud-sdk:latest
        oidc: true
        name: Metadata check
        script:
          - if [[ ${CHECK_METADATA_EVEREST} != "true" ]]; then printf 'Check Metadata is not enabled, exiting.'; exit; fi
          - export GCP_PROJECT_NUMBER=$GCP_SHARED_PROJECT_NUMBER
          - export workload_identity_pool_id='bitbucket-cloud'
          - export workload_identity_pool_provider_id='bitbucket-cloud-provider'
          - export SERVICE_ACCOUNT_EMAIL="svc-bitbucket-pipeline@${GCP_SHARED_PROJECT_ID}.iam.gserviceaccount.com"
          - echo -n "${BITBUCKET_STEP_OIDC_TOKEN}" > /tmp/gcp_access_token.out
          - gcloud iam workload-identity-pools create-cred-config "projects/${GCP_PROJECT_NUMBER}/locations/global/workloadIdentityPools/${workload_identity_pool_id}/providers/${workload_identity_pool_provider_id}" --credential-source-file=/tmp/gcp_access_token.out --service-account="${SERVICE_ACCOUNT_EMAIL}" --output-file=sts-creds.json
          # Gcloud auth and check
          - gcloud auth login --cred-file=`pwd`/sts-creds.json
          - gcloud config set project $CEP_QA_PROJECT_ID
          - gcloud auth configure-docker us-central1-docker.pkg.dev --quiet
          - pipe: docker://us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/$CEP_QA_PROJECT_ID/x4c/metadata-check-pipe:1.1
            variables:
              CHECK_METADATA: "${CHECK_METADATA}"
              FILE_PATH: "metadata.json"
    - step: &IAC-plan
          name: IAC-plan
          image: 
              name: ingrammicro.jfrog.io/ecomm-docker-images-local/gcp-terraform:latest
              username: $JFROG_USERNAME
              password: $JFROG_APIKEY
          oidc: true
          condition:
            changesets:
                includePaths: 
                  - IAC/**
                  - metadata.json
          script:
            - if [[ ${CHECK_METADATA_EVEREST} != "true" ]]; then printf 'Check Metadata is not enabled, exiting.'; exit; fi
            - apt-get update; apt-get install jq -y;
            - bash replace.sh
            - cd IAC/datadog
            - cat service-definition.tf
            # Gcloud auth and check
            - export GCP_PROJECT_NUMBER=$GCP_SHARED_PROJECT_NUMBER
            - export workload_identity_pool_id='bitbucket-cloud'
            - export workload_identity_pool_provider_id='bitbucket-cloud-provider'
            - export SERVICE_ACCOUNT_EMAIL="svc-bitbucket-pipeline@${GCP_SHARED_PROJECT_ID}.iam.gserviceaccount.com"
            - echo -n "${BITBUCKET_STEP_OIDC_TOKEN}" > /tmp/gcp_access_token.out
            - gcloud iam workload-identity-pools create-cred-config "projects/${GCP_PROJECT_NUMBER}/locations/global/workloadIdentityPools/${workload_identity_pool_id}/providers/${workload_identity_pool_provider_id}" --credential-source-file=/tmp/gcp_access_token.out --service-account="${SERVICE_ACCOUNT_EMAIL}" --output-file=sts-creds.json
            - gcloud auth login --cred-file=`pwd`/sts-creds.json
            - gcloud config set project ${GCP_SHARED_PROJECT_ID}
            - terraform init
            - terraform validate
            - terraform plan
    - step: &IAC-apply
          name: IAC-apply
          image: 
              name: ingrammicro.jfrog.io/ecomm-docker-images-local/gcp-terraform:latest
              username: $JFROG_USERNAME
              password: $JFROG_APIKEY
          condition:
            changesets:
                includePaths: 
                  - IAC/**
                  - metadata.json
          oidc: true
          script:
            - if [[ ${CHECK_METADATA_EVEREST} != "true" ]]; then printf 'Check Metadata is not enabled, exiting.'; exit; fi
            - apt-get update; apt-get install jq -y;
            - bash replace.sh
            - cd IAC/datadog
            - cat service-definition.tf
            # Gcloud auth and check
            - export GCP_PROJECT_NUMBER=$GCP_SHARED_PROJECT_NUMBER
            - export workload_identity_pool_id='bitbucket-cloud'
            - export workload_identity_pool_provider_id='bitbucket-cloud-provider'
            - export SERVICE_ACCOUNT_EMAIL="svc-bitbucket-pipeline@${GCP_SHARED_PROJECT_ID}.iam.gserviceaccount.com"
            - echo -n "${BITBUCKET_STEP_OIDC_TOKEN}" > /tmp/gcp_access_token.out
            - gcloud iam workload-identity-pools create-cred-config "projects/${GCP_PROJECT_NUMBER}/locations/global/workloadIdentityPools/${workload_identity_pool_id}/providers/${workload_identity_pool_provider_id}" --credential-source-file=/tmp/gcp_access_token.out --service-account="${SERVICE_ACCOUNT_EMAIL}" --output-file=sts-creds.json
            - gcloud auth login --cred-file=`pwd`/sts-creds.json
            - gcloud config set project ${GCP_SHARED_PROJECT_ID}
            - terraform init
            - terraform validate
            - terraform plan
            - terraform apply -auto-approve
    - step: &checkmarx
          image: google/cloud-sdk:latest
          caches:
          - docker
          oidc: true
          name: Checkmarx Analysis pipe
          script:
            - export GCP_PROJECT_NUMBER=$GCP_SHARED_PROJECT_NUMBER
            - export workload_identity_pool_id='bitbucket-cloud'
            - export workload_identity_pool_provider_id='bitbucket-cloud-provider'
            - export SERVICE_ACCOUNT_EMAIL="svc-bitbucket-pipeline@${GCP_SHARED_PROJECT_ID}.iam.gserviceaccount.com"
            - echo -n "${BITBUCKET_STEP_OIDC_TOKEN}" > /tmp/gcp_access_token.out
            - gcloud iam workload-identity-pools create-cred-config "projects/${GCP_PROJECT_NUMBER}/locations/global/workloadIdentityPools/${workload_identity_pool_id}/providers/${workload_identity_pool_provider_id}" --credential-source-file=/tmp/gcp_access_token.out --service-account="${SERVICE_ACCOUNT_EMAIL}" --output-file=sts-creds.json
            # Gcloud auth and check
            - gcloud auth login --cred-file=`pwd`/sts-creds.json
            - gcloud config set project $CEP_QA_PROJECT_ID
            - gcloud auth configure-docker us-central1-docker.pkg.dev --quiet
            - pipe: docker://us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/$CEP_QA_PROJECT_ID/x4c/checkmarx-pipe:latest
              variables:
                CHECKMARX_DEBUG_MODE: $CHECKMARX_DEBUG_MODE
                CHECKMARX_CLIENT_ID: $CHECKMARX_CLIENT_ID
                CHECKMARX_CLIENT_SECRET: $CHECKMARX_CLIENT_SECRET
                CHECKMARX_PROJECT_ID: $CHECKMARX_PROJECT_ID
                CHECKMARX_SYNC: $CHECKMARX_SYNC
                CHECKMARX_SCAN_TIMEOUT: $CHECKMARX_SCAN_TIMEOUT
                SCAN_ORIGIN: Bitbucket
                TARGET_DIRECTORY: $BITBUCKET_CLONE_DIR
                BRANCH: $BITBUCKET_BRANCH
                PIPELINE_ID: $BITBUCKET_BUILD_NUMBER
                COMMIT_HASH: $BITBUCKET_COMMIT
                PULL_REQUEST_ID: $BITBUCKET_PR_ID
                REPOSITORY_URL: https://bitbucket.org/$BITBUCKET_WORKSPACE/$BITBUCKET_REPO_SLUG
                PULL_REQUEST_DECORATOR_USERNAME: $SHIFTLEFT_BITBUCKET_USERNAME
                PULL_REQUEST_DECORATOR_SECRET: $SHIFTLEFT_BITBUCKET_APPPASSWORD

    - step: &BuildDocker
          name: Build Docker Image
          image: google/cloud-sdk:latest
          oidc: true
          caches:
            - docker
          script:
            - export GCP_PROJECT_NUMBER=$GCP_SHARED_PROJECT_NUMBER
            - export workload_identity_pool_id='bitbucket-cloud'
            - export workload_identity_pool_provider_id='bitbucket-cloud-provider'
            - export SERVICE_ACCOUNT_EMAIL="svc-bitbucket-pipeline@${GCP_SHARED_PROJECT_ID}.iam.gserviceaccount.com"
            - echo -n "${BITBUCKET_STEP_OIDC_TOKEN}" > /tmp/gcp_access_token.out
            - gcloud iam workload-identity-pools create-cred-config "projects/${GCP_PROJECT_NUMBER}/locations/global/workloadIdentityPools/${workload_identity_pool_id}/providers/${workload_identity_pool_provider_id}" --credential-source-file=/tmp/gcp_access_token.out --service-account="${SERVICE_ACCOUNT_EMAIL}" --output-file=sts-creds.json
            # Gcloud auth and check
            - gcloud auth login --cred-file=`pwd`/sts-creds.json
            - gcloud config set project ${AGENT_AI_DEV_PROJECT_ID}
            - export DEV_IMAGE=us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/$AGENT_AI_DEV_PROJECT_ID/agentai/$BITBUCKET_REPO_SLUG:${BITBUCKET_COMMIT::7}
            - curl -s -S --user $BITBUCKET_USERNAME:$BITBUCKET_APP_PASSWORD -L -O https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/imonline/branchanddeploymentautomation/downloads/.env
            - docker build -f ./Dockerfile -t $DEV_IMAGE .
            - echo "Docker image $DEV_IMAGE built successfully"
            # authenticate to image registry with gcloud helper
            - gcloud auth configure-docker us-central1-docker.pkg.dev
            - if (gcloud artifacts repositories list --location=us-central1 --project=${AGENT_AI_DEV_PROJECT_ID} | grep "agentai"); then echo "Artifact Registry Repo Already exists"; else gcloud artifacts repositories create "agentai" --repository-format=docker --location=us-central1 --project=${AGENT_AI_DEV_PROJECT_ID} | echo "Created the Repository" ; fi
            - docker push $DEV_IMAGE
            - echo "$DEV_IMAGE image has been pushed to GCR"
          services:
            -  docker
pipelines:
  default:
      - step: *MetadataCheck
      - step: *checkmarx
      #- step: *IAC-plan
  pull-requests:
      '**': #this runs as default for any branch not elsewhere defined in this script
      - step: *MetadataCheck
      - step: *checkmarx
      #- step: *IAC-plan
  branches:
    master:
      - step: *MetadataCheck
      - step: *BuildDocker
      #- step: *IAC-apply

--- IAC/datadog/provider.tf ---
terraform {
  required_providers {
    datadog = {
      source = "DataDog/datadog"
      version = "3.16.0"
    }
  }
}
provider "datadog" {
    api_key = "${var.dd_api_key}"
    app_key = "${var.dd_app_key}"
    api_url = "${var.dd_api_url}"
} 
terraform {
  backend "gcs" {
    bucket = "datadog-service-catalog"
    prefix = "%GCP_CLOUDRUN_SERVICE_NAME%"
    credentials = "sts-creds.json"
  }
}
provider "google" {
  project = "${var.dd_project}"
  credentials = "${file("sts-creds.json")}"
}
provider "google-beta" {
  user_project_override = true
  credentials = "${file("sts-creds.json")}"
}


--- IAC/datadog/service-definition.tf ---
resource "datadog_service_definition_yaml" "%TF_SERVICE_CATALOG_NAME%" {
  service_definition = <<EOF
schema-version: v2
dd-service: %VAR_BITBUCKET_REPO_SLUG_PASCAL%
team: %XVANTAGE_TEAM_NAME%
contacts:
  - name: Support Email
    type: email
    contact:  %XVANTAGE_TEAM_EMAIL_ADDRESS%
repos:
  - name: %VAR_BITBUCKET_REPO_SLUG_PASCAL%
    provider: bitbucket
    url: https://bitbucket.org/imonline/%VAR_BITBUCKET_REPO_SLUG_PASCAL%/src/master
docs:
  - name: %VAR_BITBUCKET_REPO_SLUG_PASCAL%
    provider: wiki
    url: https://bitbucket.org/imonline/%VAR_BITBUCKET_REPO_SLUG_PASCAL%/src/master/README.md
tags:
  - team_name:%XVANTAGE_TEAM_NAME% 
  - service_name:%VAR_BITBUCKET_REPO_SLUG_PASCAL%
EOF
}
resource "datadog_service_definition_yaml" "%TF_SERVICE_CATALOG_NAME%_gcp" {
  service_definition = <<EOF
schema-version: v2
dd-service: %VAR_BITBUCKET_REPO_SLUG_PASCAL%.gcp
team: %XVANTAGE_TEAM_NAME%
contacts:
  - name: Support Email
    type: email
    contact:  %XVANTAGE_TEAM_EMAIL_ADDRESS%
repos:
  - name: %VAR_BITBUCKET_REPO_SLUG_PASCAL%
    provider: bitbucket
    url: https://bitbucket.org/imonline/%VAR_BITBUCKET_REPO_SLUG_PASCAL%/src/master
docs:
  - name: %VAR_BITBUCKET_REPO_SLUG_PASCAL%
    provider: wiki
    url: https://bitbucket.org/imonline/%VAR_BITBUCKET_REPO_SLUG_PASCAL%/src/master/README.md
tags:
  - team_name:%XVANTAGE_TEAM_NAME% 
  - service_name:%VAR_BITBUCKET_REPO_SLUG_PASCAL%.gcp
EOF
}

=== 🛠️ GCP SKILLS REGISTRY STANDARDS & PLAYBOOKS ===
The following authoritative skills and standards were retrieved from the Skill Registry and must be strictly enforced during the review process.

### Skill: agent-platform-prompt-management
**Description**: Manages and orchestrates prompts in Agent Platform. Use when you need to create, list, retrieve, version, or delete managed prompts in Agent Platform. Don't use for model training, model deployment to endpoints, or managing non-Agent Platform prompts.

**Core Instructions & Scoring Criteria**:
## Usage Guide

To use this skill effectively:

1.  **Generate Code**: Provide the Python snippets below to the user to help
    them manage prompts in Agent Platform.

2.  **No File System Search**: Do not try to find Python files or scripts on the
    file system for these operations.

## Safety & Confirmation Tiers (CRITICAL)

Before executing any commands or scripts on behalf of the user, you must adhere
to the following safety tiers based on the action requested, to prevent
accidental mutation or permanent deletion of prompt resources:

1.  **Tier R: Read-only (`list`, `get`)**
    *   No confirmation needed. Execute immediately to gather information.
2.  **Tier M: Mutating & Reversible (`create`)**

    *   Requires **interactive confirmation** with 'Yes'/'No' options before
        executing prompt creation, to prevent unintended resource proliferation
        or misconfiguration. The confirmation prompt must clearly explain the
        proposed prompt creation and its key parameters (e.g., display name,
        template text, target model). Natural-language paraphrases without
        specifying the parameters are not sufficient.
    *   **Same-turn restriction**: Do not execute the creation code in the same
        turn as presenting the confirmation prompt. Stop and wait for the user's
        reply; only execute after explicit 'Yes' / approval.
    *   Every parameter in the card must trace back to something the user said.
        The target model is a user choice, not a default: if the user did not
        name one, ASK before building the card. Do not carry over the model that
        appears in the examples here or in `references/create.md`.
    *   **Gold Standard Example** — for a user who said "create a prompt called
        Customer Support Greeting for gemini-2.5-pro with the template Hello
        {{user_name}}, how can I help...":

        > I will create a prompt in Agent Platform with the following
        > parameters. Please confirm this information before I proceed:
        >
        > *   **Display Name**: `Customer Support Greeting`
        > *   **Target Model**: `gemini-2.5-pro`
        > *   **Template Text**: "Hello {{user_name}}, how can I help..."
        >
        > Do you confirm? [Yes/No]

3.  **Tier D: Destructive & Irreversible (`delete`)**

    *   Requires **explicit typed confirmation** (e.g. "I confirm" or "Yes,
        delete it") before executing prompt deletion, to prevent accidental
        permanent loss of production prompt assets. Ask for confirmation before
        any pre-flight checks.
    *   **Same-turn restriction**: NEVER execute in the same turn as asking for
        typed confirmation. Wait for the user to reply in a new turn.
    *   **Gold Standard Example**:

        > I will permanently delete the following prompt from Agent Platform.
        > This action is irreversible. Please explicitly type your confirmation
        > (e.g., "I confirm") before I proceed:
        >
        > *   **Prompt ID**: `prompt_12345abc`
        > *   **Display Name**: `Legacy Outdated Prompt`
        >
        > Please type your confirmation to proceed.

## Phase 0: Environment Setup

**CRITICAL**: Before the user runs any of the Python snippets below, you MUST
advise them to ensure the environment is correctly initialized by following
these steps:

1.  **Google Cloud Authentication**: Authenticate with your Google Cloud account
    and configure active Application Default Credentials (ADC) for Agent
    Platform access:

    ```bash
    gcloud auth login
    gcloud auth application-default login
    ```

2.  **Python Dependencies**: This skill needs `google-cloud-aiplatform` and
    `google-genai`. Do **not** create a virtual environment — it starts empty
    and hides packages the environment already provides, forcing a redundant
    install. Probe, and install only what is missing:

    ```bash
    python3 -c "import vertexai, google.genai" \
      || pip install google-cloud-aiplatform google-genai
    ```

3.  **Execution**: Run Python snippets with a plain `python3`. There is no
    environment to activate first.

> [!TIP]
>
> **Placeholder Parameter Replacement:** The Python scripts below use uppercase
> string placeholders (like `"PROJECT_ID"`, `"LOCATION_ID"`, `"PROMPT_ID"`, and
> `"MODEL_ID"`). You **MUST** dynamically replace these placeholders with the
> actual Project ID, Region, Prompt ID, and target model values provided in the
> user's prompt (or discovered context) before generating or providing the
> scripts. If the user did not supply one of these, ask -- a placeholder is
> never satisfied by guessing a plausible value.

## 1. Managing Prompts via Agent Platform SDK

The SDK provides a high-level `Prompt` class in the preview module.

### Create a Prompt (Tier M)

Use when you need to create a new managed prompt in Agent Platform.

*   **Reference**: See [create.md](references/create.md) for detailed
    instructions and Python snippets.

### List Prompts (Tier R)

```python
import vertexai
from vertexai.preview import prompts

vertexai.init(project="PROJECT_ID", location="LOCATION_ID")

all_prompts = prompts.list()
for p in all_prompts:
    print(f"Name: {p.display_name}, ID: {p.prompt_id}")
```

### Retrieve and Use a Prompt (Tier R)

```python
import vertexai
from vertexai.preview import prompts

vertexai.init(project="PROJECT_ID", location="LOCATION_ID")

retrieved_prompt = prompts.get(prompt_id="PROMPT_ID")
# Versions are supported: prompts.get(prompt_id="PROMPT_ID", version_id="2")

# Assemble with variables (kwargs must match template variable names)
assembled = retrieved_prompt.assemble_contents(text="The quick brown fox...")
print(assembled)
```

### Delete a Prompt (Tier D)

**CRITICAL**: You must pass the numeric prompt ID (e.g.,
`"1234567890123456789"`) to `prompts.delete()`. The SDK constructs the full
resource path internally using the project and location from `vertexai.init()`.

**Confirmation Required**: As a Tier D (Destructive) operation, the agent MUST
pause and request explicit, high-friction typed re-confirmation of the prompt ID
from the user before generating or providing the deletion code. The action is
irreversible.

> [!IMPORTANT]
>
> **NEVER pre-emptively provide or execute any deletion code before receiving
> the user's response in a new turn.** You must never speculate or assume that
> confirmation will be given. Asking for confirmation and providing the code in
> a single parallel turn is a severe safety violation.

```python
import vertexai
from vertexai.preview import prompts

vertexai.init(project="PROJECT_ID", location="LOCATION_ID")

prompts.delete(prompt_id="PROMPT_ID")
```

## 2. Best Practices

-   **Idempotency**:
    *   **Tier R** (List, Get): Inherently idempotent.
    *   **Tier D** (Delete): Re-running a delete on a non-existent or already
        deleted resource returns NOT_FOUND. Treat this as success.
-   **Placeholders**: Use the standard placeholder syntax (variable name
    enclosed in double curly braces) in your prompt templates.
-   **Versioning**: Always tag or record version IDs when making updates to
    production prompts.
-   **Model Reference**: A prompt is created against a target model ID, which
    the snippets carry as the `"MODEL_ID"` placeholder. Like the other
    placeholders it is MUST-replace, and it is replaced from what the user
    said -- if they named no model, ask. Do not substitute a plausible current
    model such as `gemini-2.5-pro`.
-   **Underlying Schema**: When using the Dataset API, always use the correct
    `metadata_schema_uri` and nested `metadata` structure to ensure the prompt
    is recognized by Agent Platform Studio and the Prompts SDK.

**Reference Materials**:
#### Reference File: `references/create.md`

# Creating Prompts in Agent Platform

This guide provides instructions on how to create a new managed prompt in
Agent Platform.

## Create a Prompt (Tier M)

**Confirmation Required**: As a Tier M (Mutating) operation, the agent MUST
pause and present a confirmation prompt with the project, region, prompt display
name, and model before providing the creation code.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Interactive Confirmation Required (Tier M):** Before proceeding with prompt
> creation, you **MUST** present the proposed Python code in a confirmation
> prompt to the user with 'Yes' and 'No' options.
> **CRITICAL:** When presenting this confirmation prompt to the user, you MUST
> output it as a direct plain text response and stop tool execution immediately.
> Do NOT call any command execution or interactive tools in the same turn, as
> unexpected tool calls may be auto-replied by the simulation harness and cause
> an infinite loop. Yield immediately for the user's reply.

```python
import vertexai
from vertexai.preview import prompts
from vertexai.preview.prompts import Prompt

vertexai.init(project="PROJECT_ID", location="LOCATION_ID")

# Construct a local Prompt object. `prompt_name` is the display name shown
# in Agent Platform Studio; `prompt_data` is the prompt text/template
# (use `{variable_name}` placeholders for variables passed to
# `assemble_contents()`); `model_name` is the target model -- ask the user
# which model to use, do not default to whatever this example happens to show.
local_prompt = Prompt(
    prompt_name="my_new_prompt",
    prompt_data="Hello, how are you? {text}",
    model_name="MODEL_ID",
)

# Persist the local Prompt as a new managed prompt resource. This creates
# the prompt AND its first version in a single call. The returned
# `persisted_prompt` is a Prompt object with `prompt_id` and `version_id`
# populated.
persisted_prompt = prompts.create_version(prompt=local_prompt)
print(f"Created prompt ID: {persisted_prompt.prompt_id}")
print(f"Version ID: {persisted_prompt.version_id}")
```

## 🧹 Code Quality Review

### Summary
The codebase was evaluated for code readability, maintainability, architectural cleanliness, modularity, and adherence to Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC) and containerization best practices. While the repository follows modern service containerization and Bitbucket OIDC patterns, several significant code quality, maintainability, and configuration hygiene issues were identified in the Terraform files, Dockerfile, and CI/CD pipelines.

---

### 📘 Standard: Agent Platform Prompt Management (`agent-platform-prompt-management`)
_No managed Vertex AI prompt orchestration resources are directly created or mutated in the static infrastructure/configuration files under review._

---

### Findings

#### **[High] `IAC/datadog/variables.tf:1-7` — Missing Type Constraints, Descriptions, and Sensitive Annotations in Terraform Variables**
- **Rule**: Built-in baseline / Terraform Standard Practice: All Terraform variable definitions must specify explicit `type` constraints, informative `description` fields, and `sensitive = true` for credentials and API keys to prevent state leakage and accidental type coercion.
- **Problem**: `dd_project`, `dd_api_key`, and `dd_app_key` are declared as empty blocks without types or descriptions. Sensitive keys (`dd_api_key`, `dd_app_key`) lack the `sensitive = true` attribute, which causes plain-text exposure in execution plan logs.
- **Before**:
```hcl
variable "dd_project" {}
variable "dd_api_key" {}
variable "dd_app_key" {}
variable "dd_api_url" {
    default = "https://api.%DD_SITE%/" 
}
```
- **After**:
```hcl
variable "dd_project" {
  type        = string
  description = "Target Google Cloud Project ID for Datadog integration."
}

variable "dd_api_key" {
  type        = string
  description = "Datadog API key for authentication."
  sensitive   = true
}

variable "dd_app_key" {
  type        = string
  description = "Datadog Application key for authentication."
  sensitive   = true
}

variable "dd_api_url" {
  type        = string
  description = "Datadog API intake URL."
  default     = "https://api.datadoghq.com/"
}
```
- **Why better**: Enforces strict input validation, prevents secret values from being logged in CI/CD stdout during `terraform plan/apply`, and documents variable intent.

#### **[Medium] `IAC/datadog/provider.tf:1-25` — Duplicate `terraform` Blocks and Deprecated String Interpolation Syntax**

Legacy Terraform 0.11 interpolation syntax (`"${var.foo}"`) must be replaced with native HCL expressions (`var.foo`).
- **Problem**: `provider.tf` defines two separate `terraform {}` blocks (lines 1–8 and lines 13–19) and uses deprecated `${var.dd_*}` and `${file(...)}` wrapped strings.

```hcl
terraform {
  required_providers {
    datadog = {
      source = "DataDog/datadog"
      version = "3.16.0"
    }

}

    api_key = "${var.dd_api_key}"
    app_key = "${var.dd_app_key}"

terraform {

provider "google" {
```

- **After**:
```hcl
terraform {
  required_version = ">= 1.5.0"
  required_providers {
    datadog = {
      source  = "DataDog/datadog"
      version = "~> 3.16.0"
    }
    google = {
      source  = "hashicorp/google"
      version = "~> 5.0"
    }
    google-beta = {
      source  = "hashicorp/google-beta"
      version = "~> 5.0"
    }

  backend "gcs" {
    bucket = "datadog-service-catalog"

  api_key = var.dd_api_key
  app_key = var.dd_app_key
  api_url = var.dd_api_url
}

provider "google" {
  project = var.dd_project
}

provider "google-beta" {
  project               = var.dd_project
  user_project_override = true
}
```

#### **[Medium] `bitbucket-pipelines.yml:1-30` — Top-Level Runtime Image Mismatch & Repetitive WIF Authentication Logic**

Furthermore, identical 10-line Workload Identity Federation (WIF) credential configuration scripts are copy-pasted across `MetadataCheck`, `IAC-plan`, `IAC-apply`, `checkmarx`, and `BuildDocker`.

```yaml
  depth: full 
definitions:

  steps:
```

```yaml
  depth: full

definitions:
```

## 🔒 Security & Deployment Review

### Summary
Security posture overview: **Audit conducted against Built-in Security Baselines (OWASP Top 10, CWE Top 25, Docker & Cloud Run Hardening, and GCP IAM Best Practices)**. 

The audit identified critical vulnerabilities and deployment misconfigurations across container build configurations, CI/CD pipeline artifact management, Dockerfile packaging, and Terraform Infrastructure-as-Code definitions. Most notably:
1. Cleartext authentication/authorization tokens are passed as build arguments and persisted as image environment variables (`ARG`/`ENV`).
2. Sensitive `.env` files and Workload Identity STS credentials files (`sts-creds.json`) are generated in the root workspace without `.gitignore` / `.dockerignore` containment.
3. The container image fails to package the core `agent_guardian` application module, leading to fatal startup failures on Cloud Run.
4. Datadog IaC definitions expose sensitive keys in plan logs and rely on hardcoded local credential file paths.

---

### Findings

#### **[Critical] `Dockerfile:5-9` — Sensitive Authentication & Authorization Tokens Embedded in Container Environment (`ARG`/`ENV`)**
- **Rule**: `[Built-in baseline: OWASP A02:2021 – Cryptographic Failures / CWE-526: Exposure of Sensitive Information Through Environmental Variables / CWE-200]` Secrets, API keys, and authentication/authorization tokens must never be declared via Dockerfile `ARG`/`ENV` directives or baked into container image layers.
- **Threat**: Declaring `ARG DEV_GNE_AUTHENTICATION_TOKEN` and `ARG DEV_GNE_AUTHORIZATION_TOKEN` and assigning them to `ENV` permanently bakes cleartext authorization tokens into image layer metadata and build history. Anyone with read access to the Artifact Registry repository (`docker inspect`, `docker history`, or registry pull) can extract these tokens.
- **Fix**:
```dockerfile
# Dockerfile: Remove ARG/ENV token persistence
FROM python:3.11.9-slim-bookworm

ENV PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 \
    PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 \
    APP_HOME=/app

WORKDIR $APP_HOME

COPY requirements/container.txt ./
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r container.txt

# Copy both application modules and API gateway
COPY agent_guardian $APP_HOME/agent_guardian
COPY api $APP_HOME/api

RUN useradd -ms /bin/bash -u 10001 appuser && chown -R appuser:appuser $APP_HOME
USER appuser

CMD ["fastapi", "run", "api/main.py", "--port", "8080"]
```
- **Defense in Depth**: Retrieve sensitive credentials dynamically at runtime via Google Cloud Secret Manager or inject them as runtime environment variables directly in the Cloud Run service configuration rather than passing them during image build.

---

#### **[High] `bitbucket-pipelines.yml:118` — Sensitive `.env` File Downloaded into Root Build Context in CI/CD**
- **Rule**: `[Built-in baseline: OWASP A05:2021 – Security Misconfiguration / CWE-540: Inclusion of Sensitive Information in Source Code / Build Artifacts]` Secrets configuration files (`.env`) must not be downloaded into root build contexts where they risk unintended inclusion in Docker layers or CI/CD artifact caches.
- **Threat**: The command `curl -s -S --user $BITBUCKET_USERNAME:$BITBUCKET_APP_PASSWORD -L -O https://api.bitbucket.org/.../downloads/.env` downloads a raw `.env` file directly into the root repository workspace immediately prior to `docker build .`. Because no `.dockerignore` exists in the repository, any `COPY` command or build artifact capture can accidentally bundle production secrets into the distributed container image.
- **Fix**:
```yaml
# bitbucket-pipelines.yml: Remove curl download of .env and rely on runtime secrets injection
    - step: &BuildDocker
          name: Build Docker Image
          image: google/cloud-sdk:slim
          oidc: true
          caches:
            - docker
          script:
            - export GCP_PROJECT_NUMBER=$GCP_SHARED_PROJECT_NUMBER
            - export SERVICE_ACCOUNT_EMAIL="svc-bitbucket-pipeline@${GCP_SHARED_PROJECT_ID}.iam.gserviceaccount.com"
            - echo -n "${BITBUCKET_STEP_OIDC_TOKEN}" > /tmp/gcp_access_token.out
            - gcloud iam workload-identity-pools create-cred-config "projects/${GCP_PROJECT_NUMBER}/locations/global/workloadIdentityPools/bitbucket-cloud/providers/bitbucket-cloud-provider" --credential-source-file=/tmp/gcp_access_token.out --service-account="${SERVICE_ACCOUNT_EMAIL}" --output-file=/tmp/sts-creds.json
            - gcloud auth login --cred-file=/tmp/sts-creds.json
            - gcloud config set project ${AGENT_AI_DEV_PROJECT_ID}
            - export DEV_IMAGE=us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/$AGENT_AI_DEV_PROJECT_ID/agentai/$BITBUCKET_REPO_SLUG:${BITBUCKET_COMMIT::7}
            - docker build --no-cache -f ./Dockerfile -t $DEV_IMAGE .
            - gcloud auth configure-docker us-central1-docker.pkg.dev --quiet
            - docker push $DEV_IMAGE
            - rm -f /tmp/sts-creds.json /tmp/gcp_access_token.out
```
- **Defense in Depth**: Create a `.dockerignore` file containing `.env`, `sts-creds.json`, `.git`, `IAC/`, and all local secrets to block accidental inclusion in Docker builds.

---

#### **[High] `bitbucket-pipelines.yml:23`, `bitbucket-pipelines.yml:49`, `bitbucket-pipelines.yml:76` — Credential Configuration (`sts-creds.json`) Stored in Workspace Without `.gitignore` Coverage**
- **Rule**: `[Built-in baseline: OWASP A01:2021 – Broken Access Control / CWE-312: Cleartext Storage of Sensitive Information]` Temporary credential tokens and Workload Identity configuration files must be stored in isolated temporary directories (`/tmp`) and explicitly purged after step completion.
- **Threat**: The pipeline executes `gcloud iam workload-identity-pools create-cred-config ... --output-file=sts-creds.json` directly into the repository root directory (`pwd`). `.gitignore` does not ignore `sts-creds.json`, allowing STS token configurations to persist across build steps, risk accidental commits during automated operations, or leak into container build contexts.
- **Fix**:
```gitignore
# Add to .gitignore:
sts-creds.json
.env
*.key
*.pem
/tmp/
```
```yaml
# Update bitbucket-pipelines.yml to write creds to /tmp:
--output-file=/tmp/sts-creds.json
# Authenticate using /tmp/sts-creds.json:
- gcloud auth login --cred-file=/tmp/sts-creds.json
```
- **Defense in Depth**: Run pre-commit hooks and automated secret scanning (`gitleaks`/`trufflehog`) in CI to prevent credential leakage.

---

#### **[High] `Dockerfile:1` — Floating Unpinned Docker Base Image Tag (`python:3.11`)**
- **Rule**: `[Built-in baseline: OWASP A06:2021 – Vulnerable and Outdated Components / CWE-1104: Use of Unmaintained or Non-Deterministic Third-Party Components]` Production container images must use minimal base distributions (`-slim`), specific patch versions, and SHA256 digest pinning to ensure immutability and minimal attack surface.
- **Threat**: `FROM python:3.11` uses a full-fat Debian image containing unnecessary compilers, build utilities, and non-essential packages. Floating tags introduce non-deterministic build behavior and can pull unverified upstream updates or vulnerabilities into production.
- **Fix**:
```dockerfile
# Dockerfile: Pin to minimal slim image with digest
FROM python:3.11.9-slim-bookworm@sha256:d8bb30386ff0185fb4a4cbbf310b40e53a5c9a1758c0c4c4dc8c9a3b68ec1790
```
- **Defense in Depth**: Enable Google Cloud Artifact Registry automated vulnerability scanning to scan container images for Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) upon push.

---

#### **[Medium] `Dockerfile:14` — Missing Core Application Package (`agent_guardian`) in Container Image Copy**
- **Rule**: `[Built-in baseline: Production Readiness & Cloud Run Deployment / CWE-440: Expected Behavior Violation]` All required application modules imported by the entrypoint must be copied into the container runtime image.
- **Threat**: `Dockerfile` executes `COPY api $APP_HOME/api` but does not copy `agent_guardian`. When `api/main.py` is invoked (`fastapi run api/main.py`), it attempts to import `agent_guardian.utils.compat`, causing immediate `ModuleNotFoundError` crashes upon container startup on Cloud Run.
- **Fix**:
```dockerfile
# Dockerfile: Ensure all application packages are copied
COPY agent_guardian $APP_HOME/agent_guardian
COPY api $APP_HOME/api
```
- **Defense in Depth**: Add a container validation step in CI (`docker run --rm $DEV_IMAGE python3 -c "import api.main"`) to verify import resolution before publishing images to the registry.

---

#### **[Medium] `IAC/datadog/provider.tf:16-24` — Terraform Provider and Backend Coupled to Hardcoded Local Credential Files**
- **Rule**: `[Built-in baseline: OWASP A05:2021 – Security Misconfiguration / Terraform Best Practices]` Infrastructure-as-Code definitions should rely on ambient Google Cloud Application Default Credentials (ADC) or Workload Identity Federation instead of static file path references (`credentials = "sts-creds.json"`).
- **Threat**: Referencing `credentials = "${file("sts-creds.json")}"` causes local and remote pipeline executions to fail if the static file is missing, and discourages using standard ambient Google Cloud environment variables (`GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS`).
- **Fix**:
```hcl
# IAC/datadog/provider.tf
terraform {
  required_version = ">= 1.5.0"
  required_providers {
    datadog = {
      source  = "DataDog/datadog"
      version = "~> 3.16.0"
    }
    google = {
      source  = "hashicorp/google"
      version = "~> 5.0"
    }
    google-beta = {
      source  = "hashicorp/google-beta"
      version = "~> 5.0"
    }
  }
  backend "gcs" {
    bucket = "datadog-service-catalog"
    prefix = "%GCP_CLOUDRUN_SERVICE_NAME%"
  }
}

provider "datadog" {
  api_key = var.dd_api_key
  app_key = var.dd_app_key
  api_url = var.dd_api_url
}

provider "google" {
  project = var.dd_project
}

provider "google-beta" {
  user_project_override = true
  project               = var.dd_project
}
```
- **Defense in Depth**: Set `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` dynamically in pipeline runners to allow providers to authenticate seamlessly via ambient Workload Identity tokens without file coupling in code.

---

#### **[Low] `IAC/datadog/variables.tf:1-4` — Missing Type Constraints and `sensitive` Flags on Sensitive Terraform Variables**
- **Rule**: `[Built-in baseline: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File / Terraform Best Practices]` Sensitive Terraform input variables (API keys, application tokens) must have explicit `type = string` and `sensitive = true` declarations.
- **Threat**: Declaring `var.dd_api_key` and `var.dd_app_key` without `sensitive = true` causes Terraform to print raw API keys in plain text into CI/CD build logs during `terraform plan` and `terraform apply` executions.
- **Fix**:
```hcl
# IAC/datadog/variables.tf
variable "dd_project" {
  type        = string
  description = "Target GCP Project ID"
}

variable "dd_api_key" {
  type        = string
  description = "Datadog API Key"
  sensitive   = true
}

variable "dd_app_key" {
  type        = string
  description = "Datadog Application Key"
  sensitive   = true
}

variable "dd_api_url" {
  type        = string
  description = "Datadog API URL endpoint"
  default     = "https://api.%DD_SITE%/"
}
```
- **Defense in Depth**: Store Datadog keys in Bitbucket Secured Variables or GCP Secret Manager, preventing cleartext exposure in CI logs.

---

### Deployment Scorecard

- [x] External inputs are validated. *(Passed: Pydantic models in `api/main.py` enforce typed request validation)*

## Executive Summary
The Agent Guardian deployment exhibits critical security, reliability, and governance risks resulting in a formal **REJECTED** governance verdict (Score: 24/100). The most urgent cross-cutting vulnerability stems from plain-text authentication tokens embedded in the Docker container image via `ARG`/`ENV` variables, compounded by missing `.dockerignore` and `.gitignore` guardrails that expose STS credentials and `.env` secrets during CI/CD execution. Furthermore, the container definition fails to copy the core `agent_guardian` application module, leading to fatal startup crashes on Cloud Run, while dependencies across `requirements/container.txt` remain completely unpinned. Immediate remediation requires purging cleartext secrets from Docker layers, packaging missing source modules, pinning dependencies, and standardizing Datadog IaC definitions to use sensitive variable annotations and ambient credentials.

---

## 🧹 Code Quality
## 🧹 Code Quality Review

### Summary
The codebase was evaluated for code readability, maintainability, architectural cleanliness, modularity, and adherence to Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC) and containerization best practices. While the repository follows modern service containerization and Bitbucket OIDC patterns, several significant code quality, maintainability, and configuration hygiene issues were identified in the Terraform files, Dockerfile, and CI/CD pipelines.

---

### 📘 Standard: Agent Platform Prompt Management (`agent-platform-prompt-management`)
_No managed Vertex AI prompt orchestration resources are directly created or mutated in the static infrastructure/configuration files under review._

---

### Findings

#### **[High] `IAC/datadog/variables.tf:1-7` — Missing Type Constraints, Descriptions, and Sensitive Annotations in Terraform Variables**
- **Rule**: Built-in baseline / Terraform Standard Practice: All Terraform variable definitions must specify explicit `type` constraints, informative `description` fields, and `sensitive = true` for credentials and API keys to prevent state leakage and accidental type coercion.
- **Problem**: `dd_project`, `dd_api_key`, and `dd_app_key` are declared as empty blocks without types or descriptions. Sensitive keys (`dd_api_key`, `dd_app_key`) lack the `sensitive = true` attribute, which causes plain-text exposure in execution plan logs.
- **Before**:
```hcl
variable "dd_project" {}
variable "dd_api_key" {}
variable "dd_app_key" {}
variable "dd_api_url" {
    default = "https://api.%DD_SITE%/" 
}
```
- **After**:
```hcl
variable "dd_project" {
  type        = string
  description = "Target Google Cloud Project ID for Datadog integration."
}

variable "dd_api_key" {
  type        = string
  description = "Datadog API key for authentication."
  sensitive   = true
}

variable "dd_app_key" {
  type        = string
  description = "Datadog Application key for authentication."
  sensitive   = true
}

variable "dd_api_url" {
  type        = string
  description = "Datadog API intake URL."
  default     = "https://api.datadoghq.com/"
}
```
- **Why better**: Enforces strict input validation, prevents secret values from being logged in CI/CD stdout during `terraform plan/apply`, and documents variable intent.

---

#### **[Medium] `IAC/datadog/provider.tf:1-25` — Duplicate `terraform` Blocks and Deprecated String Interpolation Syntax**
- **Rule**: Built-in baseline / HCL Style Guide: Provider configurations must consolidate all `terraform` configuration blocks (such as `required_providers` and `backend`) into a single top-level `terraform {}` block. Legacy Terraform 0.11 interpolation syntax (`"${var.foo}"`) must be replaced with native HCL expressions (`var.foo`).
- **Problem**: `provider.tf` defines two separate `terraform {}` blocks (lines 1–8 and lines 13–19) and uses deprecated `${var.dd_*}` and `${file(...)}` wrapped strings.
- **Before**:
```hcl
terraform {
  required_providers {
    datadog = {
      source = "DataDog/datadog"
      version = "3.16.0"
    }
  }
}
provider "datadog" {
    api_key = "${var.dd_api_key}"
    app_key = "${var.dd_app_key}"
    api_url = "${var.dd_api_url}"
} 
terraform {
  backend "gcs" {
    bucket = "datadog-service-catalog"
    prefix = "%GCP_CLOUDRUN_SERVICE_NAME%"
    credentials = "sts-creds.json"
  }
}
provider "google" {
  project = "${var.dd_project}"
  credentials = "${file("sts-creds.json")}"
}
```
- **After**:
```hcl
terraform {
  required_version = ">= 1.5.0"
  required_providers {
    datadog = {
      source  = "DataDog/datadog"
      version = "~> 3.16.0"
    }
    google = {
      source  = "hashicorp/google"
      version = "~> 5.0"
    }
    google-beta = {
      source  = "hashicorp/google-beta"
      version = "~> 5.0"
    }
  }

  backend "gcs" {
    bucket = "datadog-service-catalog"
    prefix = "services/agent-guardian"
  }
}

provider "datadog" {
  api_key = var.dd_api_key
  app_key = var.dd_app_key
  api_url = var.dd_api_url
}

provider "google" {
  project = var.dd_project
}

provider "google-beta" {
  project               = var.dd_project
  user_project_override = true
}
```
- **Why better**: Eliminates redundant configuration blocks, ensures compatibility with modern Terraform HCL formatting standards, and allows ADC/WIF to handle authentication without hardcoded file paths.

Furthermore, identical 10-line Workload Identity Federation (WIF) credential configuration scripts are copy-pasted across `MetadataCheck`, `IAC-plan`, `IAC-apply`, `checkmarx`, and `BuildDocker`.

```yaml
definitions:
```

```yaml
definitions:

      export GCP_PROJECT_NUMBER=$GCP_SHARED_PROJECT_NUMBER

        --service-account="${SERVICE_ACCOUNT_EMAIL}" \
        --output-file=sts-creds.json
```

- **Why better**: Eliminates obsolete Maven runtime dependencies, reduces pipeline configuration bloat by ~40 lines, and establishes a single point of maintenance for GCP OIDC authentication.

#### **[Low] `Dockerfile:1-17` — Missing Layer Pinning and Inefficient Package Installation Pattern**
- **Rule**: Built-in baseline / Dockerfile Best Practice: Container definitions should pin base images to specific minor/patch versions (`python:3.11-slim`), avoid bundling build arguments into persistent environment variables unnecessarily, and group directory operations for optimal cache utilization.

## 🔒 Security & Deployment
## 🔒 Security & Deployment Review

### Summary
Security posture overview: **Audit conducted against Built-in Security Baselines (OWASP Top 10, CWE Top 25, Docker & Cloud Run Hardening, and GCP IAM Best Practices)**. 

The audit identified critical vulnerabilities and deployment misconfigurations across container build configurations, CI/CD pipeline artifact management, Dockerfile packaging, and Terraform Infrastructure-as-Code definitions. Most notably:
1. Cleartext authentication/authorization tokens are passed as build arguments and persisted as image environment variables (`ARG`/`ENV`).
2. Sensitive `.env` files and Workload Identity STS credentials files (`sts-creds.json`) are generated in the root workspace without `.gitignore` / `.dockerignore` containment.
3. The container image fails to package the core `agent_guardian` application module, leading to fatal startup failures on Cloud Run.
4. Datadog IaC definitions expose sensitive keys in plan logs and rely on hardcoded local credential file paths.

---

### Findings

#### **[Critical] `Dockerfile:5-9` — Sensitive Authentication & Authorization Tokens Embedded in Container Environment (`ARG`/`ENV`)**
- **Rule**: `[Built-in baseline: OWASP A02:2021 – Cryptographic Failures / CWE-526: Exposure of Sensitive Information Through Environmental Variables / CWE-200]` Secrets, API keys, and authentication/authorization tokens must never be declared via Dockerfile `ARG`/`ENV` directives or baked into container image layers.
- **Threat**: Declaring `ARG DEV_GNE_AUTHENTICATION_TOKEN` and `ARG DEV_GNE_AUTHORIZATION_TOKEN` and assigning them to `ENV` permanently bakes cleartext authorization tokens into image layer metadata and build history. Anyone with read access to the Artifact Registry repository (`docker inspect`, `docker history`, or registry pull) can extract these tokens.
- **Fix**:
```dockerfile
# Dockerfile: Remove ARG/ENV token persistence
FROM python:3.11.9-slim-bookworm

ENV PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 \
    PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 \
    APP_HOME=/app

WORKDIR $APP_HOME

COPY requirements/container.txt ./
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r container.txt

# Copy both application modules and API gateway
COPY agent_guardian $APP_HOME/agent_guardian
COPY api $APP_HOME/api

RUN useradd -ms /bin/bash -u 10001 appuser && chown -R appuser:appuser $APP_HOME
USER appuser

CMD ["fastapi", "run", "api/main.py", "--port", "8080"]
```
- **Defense in Depth**: Retrieve sensitive credentials dynamically at runtime via Google Cloud Secret Manager or inject them as runtime environment variables directly in the Cloud Run service configuration rather than passing them during image build.

---

#### **[High] `bitbucket-pipelines.yml:118` — Sensitive `.env` File Downloaded into Root Build Context in CI/CD**
- **Rule**: `[Built-in baseline: OWASP A05:2021 – Security Misconfiguration / CWE-540: Inclusion of Sensitive Information in Source Code / Build Artifacts]` Secrets configuration files (`.env`) must not be downloaded into root build contexts where they risk unintended inclusion in Docker layers or CI/CD artifact caches.
- **Threat**: The command `curl -s -S --user $BITBUCKET_USERNAME:$BITBUCKET_APP_PASSWORD -L -O https://api.bitbucket.org/.../downloads/.env` downloads a raw `.env` file directly into the root repository workspace immediately prior to `docker build .`. Because no `.dockerignore` exists in the repository, any `COPY` command or build artifact capture can accidentally bundle production secrets into the distributed container image.
- **Fix**:
```yaml
# bitbucket-pipelines.yml: Remove curl download of .env and rely on runtime secrets injection
    - step: &BuildDocker
          name: Build Docker Image
          image: google/cloud-sdk:slim
          oidc: true
          caches:
            - docker
          script:
            - export GCP_PROJECT_NUMBER=$GCP_SHARED_PROJECT_NUMBER
            - export SERVICE_ACCOUNT_EMAIL="svc-bitbucket-pipeline@${GCP_SHARED_PROJECT_ID}.iam.gserviceaccount.com"
            - echo -n "${BITBUCKET_STEP_OIDC_TOKEN}" > /tmp/gcp_access_token.out
            - gcloud iam workload-identity-pools create-cred-config "projects/${GCP_PROJECT_NUMBER}/locations/global/workloadIdentityPools/bitbucket-cloud/providers/bitbucket-cloud-provider" --credential-source-file=/tmp/gcp_access_token.out --service-account="${SERVICE_ACCOUNT_EMAIL}" --output-file=/tmp/sts-creds.json
            - gcloud auth login --cred-file=/tmp/sts-creds.json
            - gcloud config set project ${AGENT_AI_DEV_PROJECT_ID}
            - export DEV_IMAGE=us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/$AGENT_AI_DEV_PROJECT_ID/agentai/$BITBUCKET_REPO_SLUG:${BITBUCKET_COMMIT::7}
            - docker build --no-cache -f ./Dockerfile -t $DEV_IMAGE .
            - gcloud auth configure-docker us-central1-docker.pkg.dev --quiet
            - docker push $DEV_IMAGE
            - rm -f /tmp/sts-creds.json /tmp/gcp_access_token.out
```
- **Defense in Depth**: Create a `.dockerignore` file containing `.env`, `sts-creds.json`, `.git`, `IAC/`, and all local secrets to block accidental inclusion in Docker builds.

---

#### **[High] `bitbucket-pipelines.yml:23`, `bitbucket-pipelines.yml:49`, `bitbucket-pipelines.yml:76` — Credential Configuration (`sts-creds.json`) Stored in Workspace Without `.gitignore` Coverage**
- **Rule**: `[Built-in baseline: OWASP A01:2021 – Broken Access Control / CWE-312: Cleartext Storage of Sensitive Information]` Temporary credential tokens and Workload Identity configuration files must be stored in isolated temporary directories (`/tmp`) and explicitly purged after step completion.
- **Threat**: The pipeline executes `gcloud iam workload-identity-pools create-cred-config ... --output-file=sts-creds.json` directly into the repository root directory (`pwd`). `.gitignore` does not ignore `sts-creds.json`, allowing STS token configurations to persist across build steps, risk accidental commits during automated operations, or leak into container build contexts.
- **Fix**:
```gitignore
# Add to .gitignore:
sts-creds.json
.env
*.key
*.pem
/tmp/
```
```yaml
# Update bitbucket-pipelines.yml to write creds to /tmp:
--output-file=/tmp/sts-creds.json
# Authenticate using /tmp/sts-creds.json:
- gcloud auth login --cred-file=/tmp/sts-creds.json
```
- **Defense in Depth**: Run pre-commit hooks and automated secret scanning (`gitleaks`/`trufflehog`) in CI to prevent credential leakage.

---

#### **[High] `Dockerfile:1` — Floating Unpinned Docker Base Image Tag (`python:3.11`)**
- **Rule**: `[Built-in baseline: OWASP A06:2021 – Vulnerable and Outdated Components / CWE-1104: Use of Unmaintained or Non-Deterministic Third-Party Components]` Production container images must use minimal base distributions (`-slim`), specific patch versions, and SHA256 digest pinning to ensure immutability and minimal attack surface.
- **Threat**: `FROM python:3.11` uses a full-fat Debian image containing unnecessary compilers, build utilities, and non-essential packages. Floating tags introduce non-deterministic build behavior and can pull unverified upstream updates or vulnerabilities into production.
- **Fix**:
```dockerfile
# Dockerfile: Pin to minimal slim image with digest
FROM python:3.11.9-slim-bookworm@sha256:d8bb30386ff0185fb4a4cbbf310b40e53a5c9a1758c0c4c4dc8c9a3b68ec1790
```
- **Defense in Depth**: Enable Google Cloud Artifact Registry automated vulnerability scanning to scan container images for Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) upon push.

---

#### **[Medium] `Dockerfile:14` — Missing Core Application Package (`agent_guardian`) in Container Image Copy**
- **Rule**: `[Built-in baseline: Production Readiness & Cloud Run Deployment / CWE-440: Expected Behavior Violation]` All required application modules imported by the entrypoint must be copied into the container runtime image.
- **Threat**: `Dockerfile` executes `COPY api $APP_HOME/api` but does not copy `agent_guardian`. When `api/main.py` is invoked (`fastapi run api/main.py`), it attempts to import `agent_guardian.utils.compat`, causing immediate `ModuleNotFoundError` crashes upon container startup on Cloud Run.
- **Fix**:
```dockerfile
# Dockerfile: Ensure all application packages are copied
COPY agent_guardian $APP_HOME/agent_guardian
COPY api $APP_HOME/api
```
- **Defense in Depth**: Add a container validation step in CI (`docker run --rm $DEV_IMAGE python3 -c "import api.main"`) to verify import resolution before publishing images to the registry.

---

#### **[Medium] `IAC/datadog/provider.tf:16-24` — Terraform Provider and Backend Coupled to Hardcoded Local Credential Files**
- **Rule**: `[Built-in baseline: OWASP A05:2021 – Security Misconfiguration / Terraform Best Practices]` Infrastructure-as-Code definitions should rely on ambient Google Cloud Application Default Credentials (ADC) or Workload Identity Federation instead of static file path references (`credentials = "sts-creds.json"`).
- **Threat**: Referencing `credentials = "${file("sts-creds.json")}"` causes local and remote pipeline executions to fail if the static file is missing, and discourages using standard ambient Google Cloud environment variables (`GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS`).
- **Fix**:
```hcl
# IAC/datadog/provider.tf
terraform {
  required_version = ">= 1.5.0"
  required_providers {
    datadog = {
      source  = "DataDog/datadog"
      version = "~> 3.16.0"
    }
    google = {
      source  = "hashicorp/google"
      version = "~> 5.0"
    }
    google-beta = {
      source  = "hashicorp/google-beta"
      version = "~> 5.0"
    }
  }
  backend "gcs" {
    bucket = "datadog-service-catalog"
    prefix = "%GCP_CLOUDRUN_SERVICE_NAME%"
  }
}

provider "datadog" {
  api_key = var.dd_api_key
  app_key = var.dd_app_key
  api_url = var.dd_api_url
}

provider "google" {
  project = var.dd_project
}

provider "google-beta" {
  user_project_override = true
  project               = var.dd_project
}
```
- **Defense in Depth**: Set `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` dynamically in pipeline runners to allow providers to authenticate seamlessly via ambient Workload Identity tokens without file coupling in code.

---

#### **[Low] `IAC/datadog/variables.tf:1-4` — Missing Type Constraints and `sensitive` Flags on Sensitive Terraform Variables**
- **Rule**: `[Built-in baseline: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File / Terraform Best Practices]` Sensitive Terraform input variables (API keys, application tokens) must have explicit `type = string` and `sensitive = true` declarations.
- **Threat**: Declaring `var.dd_api_key` and `var.dd_app_key` without `sensitive = true` causes Terraform to print raw API keys in plain text into CI/CD build logs during `terraform plan` and `terraform apply` executions.
- **Fix**:
```hcl
# IAC/datadog/variables.tf
variable "dd_project" {
  type        = string
  description = "Target GCP Project ID"
}

variable "dd_api_key" {
  type        = string
  description = "Datadog API Key"
  sensitive   = true
}

variable "dd_app_key" {
  type        = string
  description = "Datadog Application Key"
  sensitive   = true
}

variable "dd_api_url" {
  type        = string
  description = "Datadog API URL endpoint"
  default     = "https://api.%DD_SITE%/"
}
```
- **Defense in Depth**: Store Datadog keys in Bitbucket Secured Variables or GCP Secret Manager, preventing cleartext exposure in CI logs.

</script>

    <style>
        :root {
            scroll-behavior: smooth;
        }

        /* ── SCROLL PROGRESS BAR ── */
        #scroll-progress {
            position: fixed;
            top: 0;
            left: 0;
            width: 0%;
            height: 3px;
            background: linear-gradient(90deg, #0054a6, #16a34a, #0054a6);
            background-size: 200% auto;
            animation: shimmer-bar 2.5s linear infinite;
            z-index: 9999;
            transition: width 0.1s linear;
        }

        .material-symbols-outlined {
            font-variation-settings: 'FILL' 0, 'wght' 400, 'GRAD' 0, 'opsz' 24;
            vertical-align: middle;
        }

        /* ── RESPONSIVE LAYOUT (hand-written, not Tailwind utilities) ──
           The inlined Tailwind stylesheet is a STATIC file pre-compiled
           offline (tools/report_assets); it only contains the utility
           classes that existed in the template when it was last built. A
           hand-added `md:flex` / `lg:hidden` / `sm:px-8` etc. silently does
           nothing if that exact class wasn't already in the bundle — no
           error, the layout just never responds. Anything genuinely new
           must be plain CSS here instead of a new Tailwind class
           combination. */
        @media (max-width: 859px) {
            #ag-sidebar { display: none; }
            #ag-mobile-header { display: flex; }
            #ag-main { margin-left: 0; padding-top: 56px; }
            #ag-topbar { padding-left: 16px; padding-right: 16px; }
            .ag-topbar-date-group { display: none; }
        }
        @media (min-width: 860px) {
            #ag-sidebar { display: flex; }
            #ag-mobile-header { display: none; }
            #ag-main { margin-left: 16rem; padding-top: 0; }
            #ag-topbar { padding-left: 32px; padding-right: 32px; }
            .ag-topbar-date-group { display: inline-block; }
        }
        .ag-hero-title {
            font-size: 24px;
        }
        @media (min-width: 1024px) {
            .ag-hero-title { font-size: 30px; }
        }

        /* ── BRAND LOGO & BADGE SIZING (CRITICAL CONSTRAINT) ── */
        .ag-sidebar-logo {
            width: 32px !important;
            height: 32px !important;
            min-width: 32px !important;
            min-height: 32px !important;
            max-width: 32px !important;
            max-height: 32px !important;
            object-fit: contain !important;
            display: block !important;
            flex-shrink: 0 !important;
            border-radius: 8px !important;
        }
        .ag-adk-badge-box {
            width: 18px !important;
            height: 18px !important;
            min-width: 18px !important;
            min-height: 18px !important;
            max-width: 18px !important;
            max-height: 18px !important;
            display: flex !important;
            align-items: center !important;
            justify-content: center !important;
            overflow: hidden !important;
            flex-shrink: 0 !important;
            background: #ffffff !important;
            border-radius: 4px !important;
            border: 1px solid #e2e8f0 !important;
        }
        .ag-adk-badge-icon {
            width: 13px !important;
            height: 13px !important;
            min-width: 13px !important;
            min-height: 13px !important;
            max-width: 13px !important;
            max-height: 13px !important;
            object-fit: contain !important;
            display: block !important;
            flex-shrink: 0 !important;
        }
        .ag-mobile-logo {
            width: 24px !important;
            height: 24px !important;
            min-width: 24px !important;
            min-height: 24px !important;
            max-width: 24px !important;
            max-height: 24px !important;
            object-fit: contain !important;
            display: block !important;
            flex-shrink: 0 !important;
        }
        .ag-print-logo {
            width: 36px !important;
            height: 36px !important;
            min-width: 36px !important;
            min-height: 36px !important;
            max-width: 36px !important;
            max-height: 36px !important;
            object-fit: contain !important;
            display: block !important;
            flex-shrink: 0 !important;
        }
        .ag-footer-logo {
            width: 28px !important;
            height: 28px !important;
            min-width: 28px !important;
            min-height: 28px !important;
            max-width: 28px !important;
            max-height: 28px !important;
            object-fit: contain !important;
            display: block !important;
            flex-shrink: 0 !important;
        }

        /* ── GLASS PANEL SYSTEM ── */
        .glass-panel {
            background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.7);
            backdrop-filter: blur(12px);
            -webkit-backdrop-filter: blur(12px);
            border: 1px solid rgba(226, 232, 240, 0.8);
            transition: transform 0.25s cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1), box-shadow 0.25s cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1);
            box-shadow: 0 4px 18px rgba(0, 44, 119, 0.05);
        }
        .glass-panel:hover {
            transform: translateY(-2px);
            box-shadow: 0 10px 25px rgba(0, 44, 119, 0.1);
            border-color: rgba(0, 84, 166, 0.2);
        }

        /* ── ACTIVE NAV STATE ── */
        .nav-link {
            position: relative;
            transition: all 0.25s ease;
            color: #475569 !important;
        }
        .nav-link:hover {
            color: #0f172a !important;
            background: #f1f5f9;
        }
        .nav-link-active {
            background: rgba(0, 84, 166, 0.08) !important;
            color: #0054a6 !important;
            font-weight: 700;
        }
        .nav-link-active::before {
            content: '';
            position: absolute;
            left: 0;
            top: 15%;
            width: 4px;
            height: 70%;
            background: #0054a6;
            border-radius: 0 4px 4px 0;
        }
        .nav-link-active .material-symbols-outlined {
            font-variation-settings: 'FILL' 1;
            color: #0054a6 !important;
        }

        /* ── KEYFRAME KINETICS ── */
        @keyframes shimmer-bar {
            0% { background-position: 0% 50%; }
            50% { background-position: 100% 50%; }
            100% { background-position: 0% 50%; }
        }
        @keyframes pulse-ring {
            0% { box-shadow: 0 0 0 0 rgba(220, 38, 38, 0.35); }
            70% { box-shadow: 0 0 0 8px rgba(220, 38, 38, 0); }
            100% { box-shadow: 0 0 0 0 rgba(220, 38, 38, 0); }
        }
        @keyframes pulse-ring-crit {
            0% { box-shadow: 0 0 8px rgba(220, 38, 38, 0.4), 0 0 0 0 rgba(220, 38, 38, 0.3); }
            50% { box-shadow: 0 0 16px rgba(220, 38, 38, 0.7), 0 0 8px rgba(220, 38, 38, 0.15); }
            100% { box-shadow: 0 0 8px rgba(220, 38, 38, 0.4), 0 0 0 0 rgba(220, 38, 38, 0); }
        }
        @keyframes pulse-ring-high {
            0% { box-shadow: 0 0 6px rgba(234, 88, 12, 0.3), 0 0 0 0 rgba(234, 88, 12, 0.25); }
            50% { box-shadow: 0 0 12px rgba(234, 88, 12, 0.5), 0 0 6px rgba(234, 88, 12, 0.1); }
            100% { box-shadow: 0 0 6px rgba(234, 88, 12, 0.3), 0 0 0 0 rgba(234, 88, 12, 0); }
        }
        @keyframes pulse-dot {
            0%, 100% { transform: scale(1); opacity: 1; }
            50% { transform: scale(0.7); opacity: 0.5; }
        }
        @keyframes shimmer {
            0% { background-position: -400px 0; }
            100% { background-position: 400px 0; }
        }
        @keyframes card-entrance {
            from { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(20px); }
            to { opacity: 1; transform: translateY(0); }
        }
        @keyframes flow-line {
            0% { background-position: 0% 50%; }
            100% { background-position: 200% 50%; }
        }
        .glowing-flow-line {
            background: linear-gradient(90deg, #0054a6, #16a34a, #0054a6);
            background-size: 200% 100%;
            animation: flow-line 4s linear infinite;
        }

        /* ── SEVERITY DOT ANIMATIONS ── */
        .status-chip-dot {
            width: 8px; height: 8px;
            border-radius: 50%;
            animation: pulse-dot 1.8s ease-in-out infinite;
        }

        /* ── DYNAMIC ENTRY FOR FINDINGS ── */
        .finding-card-v2 {
            border: 1px solid #e2e8f0;
            border-left-width: 4px;
            border-radius: 12px;
            background: #ffffff;
            overflow: hidden;
            transition: all 0.25s cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1);
            opacity: 0;
            transform: translateY(15px);
        }
        .finding-card-v2.card-visible {
            opacity: 1;
            transform: translateY(0);
        }
        .finding-card-v2:hover {
            border-color: rgba(0, 84, 166, 0.3);
            box-shadow: 0 10px 25px rgba(0, 44, 119, 0.08);
            transform: translateY(-2px);
        }

        /* Severity Borders & Tints (Natively Light Theme) */
        .finding-card-v2.sev-card-critical { border-left-color: #dc2626; }
        .finding-card-v2.sev-card-critical .finding-card-head { background: rgba(220, 38, 38, 0.04); }
        .finding-card-v2.sev-card-high { border-left-color: #ea580c; }
        .finding-card-v2.sev-card-high .finding-card-head { background: rgba(234, 88, 12, 0.04); }
        .finding-card-v2.sev-card-medium { border-left-color: #d97706; }
        .finding-card-v2.sev-card-medium .finding-card-head { background: rgba(217, 119, 6, 0.04); }
        .finding-card-v2.sev-card-low { border-left-color: #16a34a; }
        .finding-card-v2.sev-card-low .finding-card-head { background: rgba(22, 163, 74, 0.04); }
        .finding-card-v2.sev-card-info { border-left-color: #0054a6; }
        .finding-card-v2.sev-card-info .finding-card-head { background: rgba(0, 84, 166, 0.04); }

        .finding-card-head {
            padding: 12px 20px;
            display: flex;
            align-items: center;
            gap: 16px;
            border-bottom: 1px solid #e2e8f0;
            min-height: 60px;
        }
        .finding-title {
            font-weight: 700;
            color: #0f172a !important;
            font-size: 16px !important;
            flex-grow: 1;
            font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif;
            text-align: left;
            line-height: 1.4 !important;
        }
        .finding-num {
            width: 36px;
            flex-shrink: 0;
            font-family: ui-monospace, monospace;
            font-weight: 800;
            color: #64748b !important;
            font-size: 12px !important;
            text-align: center;
            background: #f1f5f9 !important;
            border-radius: 6px;
            padding: 2px 4px;
        }
        .finding-card-body {
            padding: 18px 20px;
            color: #475569 !important;
            font-size: 13px;
            line-height: 1.6;
            text-align: left;
        }

        /* ── EXPLAINER / ACCENT BADGES ── */
        .precision-audit-pill {
            color: #0054a6;
            font-size: 9px;
            font-weight: 900;
            letter-spacing: 0.15em;
            text-transform: uppercase;
            display: inline-flex;
            align-items: center;
            gap: 4px;
        }

        /* ── PROGRESS BARS ── */
        .animated-bar {
            height: 6px;
            border-radius: 9999px;
            width: 0%;
            transition: width 1.2s cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1);
            background: linear-gradient(90deg, #0054a6, #16a34a);
        }
        .animated-bar.bar-visible {
            width: var(--target-w);
        }

        /* ── REVEAL ON SCROLL ── */
        .reveal-on-scroll {
            opacity: 0;
            transform: translateY(15px);
            transition: opacity 0.65s cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1), transform 0.65s cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1);
        }
        .reveal-on-scroll.is-visible {
            opacity: 1;
            transform: translateY(0);
        }

        /* Custom Scrollbar */
        ::-webkit-scrollbar { width: 5px; height: 5px; }
        ::-webkit-scrollbar-track { background: #f8fafc; }
        ::-webkit-scrollbar-thumb { background: #cbd5e1; border-radius: 10px; }
        ::-webkit-scrollbar-thumb:hover { background: #94a3b8; }

        /* SCORECARD TABLE (Natively Light Theme) */
        .scorecard-table thead th {
            border-bottom: 2px solid #e2e8f0 !important;
            color: #64748b !important;
            text-align: left;
        }
        .scorecard-table tbody td {
            color: #334155 !important;
            border-bottom: 1px solid #f1f5f9 !important;
            text-align: left;
        }
        .scorecard-table tbody tr:hover td {

<h3>Summary</h3>
<p>Security posture overview: <strong>Audit conducted against Built-in Security Baselines (OWASP Top 10, CWE Top 25, Docker & Cloud Run Hardening, and GCP IAM Best Practices)</strong>. </p>
<p>The audit identified critical vulnerabilities and deployment misconfigurations across container build configurations, CI/CD pipeline artifact management, Dockerfile packaging, and Terraform Infrastructure-as-Code definitions. Most notably:
1. Cleartext authentication/authorization tokens are passed as build arguments and persisted as image environment variables (<code>ARG</code>/<code>ENV</code>).
2. Sensitive <code>.env</code> files and Workload Identity STS credentials files (<code>sts-creds.json</code>) are generated in the root workspace without <code>.gitignore</code> / <code>.dockerignore</code> containment.

<hr />
<h3>Findings</h3>
<h4><strong>[Critical] <code>Dockerfile:5-9</code> — Sensitive Authentication & Authorization Tokens Embedded in Container Environment (<code>ARG</code>/<code>ENV</code>)</strong></h4>
<ul>
<li><strong>Rule</strong>: <code>[Built-in baseline: OWASP A02:2021 – Cryptographic Failures / CWE-526: Exposure of Sensitive Information Through Environmental Variables / CWE-200]</code> Secrets, API keys, and authentication/authorization tokens must never be declared via Dockerfile <code>ARG</code>/<code>ENV</code> directives or baked into container image layers.</li>
<li><strong>Threat</strong>: Declaring <code>ARG DEV_GNE_AUTHENTICATION_TOKEN</code> and <code>ARG DEV_GNE_AUTHORIZATION_TOKEN</code> and assigning them to <code>ENV</code> permanently bakes cleartext authorization tokens into image layer metadata and build history. Anyone with read access to the Artifact Registry repository (<code>docker inspect</code>, <code>docker history</code>, or registry pull) can extract these tokens.</li>
<li><strong>Fix</strong>:</li>
</ul>
<pre><code class="language-dockerfile"># Dockerfile: Remove ARG/ENV token persistence
FROM python:3.11.9-slim-bookworm

ENV PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 \
    PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 \
    APP_HOME=/app

WORKDIR $APP_HOME

COPY requirements/container.txt ./
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r container.txt

# Copy both application modules and API gateway
COPY agent_guardian $APP_HOME/agent_guardian
COPY api $APP_HOME/api

RUN useradd -ms /bin/bash -u 10001 appuser && chown -R appuser:appuser $APP_HOME
USER appuser

CMD ["fastapi", "run", "api/main.py", "--port", "8080"]
</code></pre>
<ul>
<li><strong>Defense in Depth</strong>: Retrieve sensitive credentials dynamically at runtime via Google Cloud Secret Manager or inject them as runtime environment variables directly in the Cloud Run service configuration rather than passing them during image build.</li>
</ul>

<h4><strong>[High] <code>bitbucket-pipelines.yml:118</code> — Sensitive <code>.env</code> File Downloaded into Root Build Context in CI/CD</strong></h4>
<ul>
<li><strong>Rule</strong>: <code>[Built-in baseline: OWASP A05:2021 – Security Misconfiguration / CWE-540: Inclusion of Sensitive Information in Source Code / Build Artifacts]</code> Secrets configuration files (<code>.env</code>) must not be downloaded into root build contexts where they risk unintended inclusion in Docker layers or CI/CD artifact caches.</li>
<li><strong>Threat</strong>: The command <code>curl -s -S --user $BITBUCKET_USERNAME:$BITBUCKET_APP_PASSWORD -L -O https://api.bitbucket.org/.../downloads/.env</code> downloads a raw <code>.env</code> file directly into the root repository workspace immediately prior to <code>docker build .</code>. Because no <code>.dockerignore</code> exists in the repository, any <code>COPY</code> command or build artifact capture can accidentally bundle production secrets into the distributed container image.</li>
<li><strong>Fix</strong>:</li>
</ul>
<pre><code class="language-yaml"># bitbucket-pipelines.yml: Remove curl download of .env and rely on runtime secrets injection
    - step: &BuildDocker
          name: Build Docker Image
          image: google/cloud-sdk:slim
          oidc: true
          caches:
            - docker
          script:
            - export GCP_PROJECT_NUMBER=$GCP_SHARED_PROJECT_NUMBER
            - export SERVICE_ACCOUNT_EMAIL="svc-bitbucket-pipeline@${GCP_SHARED_PROJECT_ID}.iam.gserviceaccount.com"
            - echo -n "${BITBUCKET_STEP_OIDC_TOKEN}" > /tmp/gcp_access_token.out
            - gcloud iam workload-identity-pools create-cred-config "projects/${GCP_PROJECT_NUMBER}/locations/global/workloadIdentityPools/bitbucket-cloud/providers/bitbucket-cloud-provider" --credential-source-file=/tmp/gcp_access_token.out --service-account="${SERVICE_ACCOUNT_EMAIL}" --output-file=/tmp/sts-creds.json
            - gcloud auth login --cred-file=/tmp/sts-creds.json
            - gcloud config set project ${AGENT_AI_DEV_PROJECT_ID}
            - export DEV_IMAGE=us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/$AGENT_AI_DEV_PROJECT_ID/agentai/$BITBUCKET_REPO_SLUG:${BITBUCKET_COMMIT::7}
            - docker build --no-cache -f ./Dockerfile -t $DEV_IMAGE .
            - gcloud auth configure-docker us-central1-docker.pkg.dev --quiet
            - docker push $DEV_IMAGE
            - rm -f /tmp/sts-creds.json /tmp/gcp_access_token.out
</code></pre>
<ul>
<li><strong>Defense in Depth</strong>: Create a <code>.dockerignore</code> file containing <code>.env</code>, <code>sts-creds.json</code>, <code>.git</code>, <code>IAC/</code>, and all local secrets to block accidental inclusion in Docker builds.</li>
</ul>
<hr />
<h4><strong>[High] <code>bitbucket-pipelines.yml:23</code>, <code>bitbucket-pipelines.yml:49</code>, <code>bitbucket-pipelines.yml:76</code> — Credential Configuration (<code>sts-creds.json</code>) Stored in Workspace Without <code>.gitignore</code> Coverage</strong></h4>
<ul>
<li><strong>Rule</strong>: <code>[Built-in baseline: OWASP A01:2021 – Broken Access Control / CWE-312: Cleartext Storage of Sensitive Information]</code> Temporary credential tokens and Workload Identity configuration files must be stored in isolated temporary directories (<code>/tmp</code>) and explicitly purged after step completion.</li>
<li><strong>Threat</strong>: The pipeline executes <code>gcloud iam workload-identity-pools create-cred-config ... --output-file=sts-creds.json</code> directly into the repository root directory (<code>pwd</code>). <code>.gitignore</code> does not ignore <code>sts-creds.json</code>, allowing STS token configurations to persist across build steps, risk accidental commits during automated operations, or leak into container build contexts.</li>
<li><strong>Fix</strong>:</li>
</ul>
<pre><code class="language-gitignore"># Add to .gitignore:
sts-creds.json
.env
*.key
*.pem
/tmp/
</code></pre>
<pre><code class="language-yaml"># Update bitbucket-pipelines.yml to write creds to /tmp:
--output-file=/tmp/sts-creds.json
# Authenticate using /tmp/sts-creds.json:
- gcloud auth login --cred-file=/tmp/sts-creds.json
</code></pre>
<ul>
<li><strong>Defense in Depth</strong>: Run pre-commit hooks and automated secret scanning (<code>gitleaks</code>/<code>trufflehog</code>) in CI to prevent credential leakage.</li>

        // Score Circle Animation with counter
        function animateScore() {
            const scoreValEl = document.getElementById('score-val');
            const ring       = document.getElementById('health-ring');
            if (!ring || !scoreValEl) return;

            const finalScore   = parseInt(scoreValEl.dataset.score || scoreValEl.innerText || '0', 10);
            const circumference = 2 * Math.PI * 58; // r=58
            const offset       = circumference - (finalScore / 100) * circumference;

            let color = '#dc2626'; // red (critical)
            if      (finalScore >= 90) color = '#16a34a'; // green
            else if (finalScore >= 70) color = '#0054a6'; // brand blue
            else if (finalScore >= 40) color = '#d97706'; // amber

            ring.style.stroke = color;
            setTimeout(() => { ring.style.strokeDashoffset = offset; }, 300);

            // Animated counter
            scoreValEl.innerText = '0';
            let start = null;
            const dur = 1400;
            function step(ts) {
                if (!start) start = ts;
                const pct  = Math.min((ts - start) / dur, 1);
                const ease = 1 - Math.pow(1 - pct, 3); // easeOutCubic
                scoreValEl.innerText = Math.round(ease * finalScore);
                if (pct < 1) requestAnimationFrame(step);
                else scoreValEl.innerText = finalScore;
            }
            setTimeout(() => requestAnimationFrame(step), 400);
